title: Beta program access policy change — internal announce draft
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

- This is a scratch draft for the internal announce + FAQ around the change to our beta access policy for hosted models and early-feature enrollment. Goal: align eng/product/CS on messaging before we post to customers and update the sign-up flows.

Key change (one-liner):
- We are moving from an invite-only beta pool to a tiered self-serve beta model: Public waitlist -> Early access (opt-in self-serve) -> Priority pilot (sales/professional services-managed).

Why we’re doing this (bullet points to use in comms):
- Reduce manual invite overhead and long customer wait times.
- Increase sign-ups and signal volume for infra sizing and model-quality evaluation.
- Make it easier for teams to try features while preserving ability to surface qualified pilots.
- Improve telemetry (we can attach explicit consent/telemetry flags during opt-in).

High-level timeline (proposed):
- Mar 23: Internal announce + prep materials (this doc + short playbook for CS/SEs).
- Mar 30: Update public docs + support KB.
- Apr 6: Behind-the-scenes migration: existing invitees get a code that auto-qualifies them into Early Access.
- Apr 13: Beta sign-up widget replaces invite-only UI.

Audience(s) to notify internally:
- CS / Customer Success (priority: messaging + how to qualify customers for Priority Pilot).
- Sales / Solutions (how to escalate customers to pilots).
- SDK and Docs (update examples for onboarding).
- Console / growth (update sign-up flows + banners).
- Legal / Privacy (final consent language + telemetry opt-in).

Draft internal Slack announcement (short):
- Heads up: we’re switching the beta program from invite-only to a tiered self-serve model to speed access and cut manual ops. Rolling out internal docs + playbook Mar 23; public-facing sign-up will be live ~Apr 6. CS/Sales: please hold off on manual invites after Apr 6 unless you’re doing a Priority Pilot. Details -> confluence link (TBD).

Draft customer-facing announcement (longer, for marketing copy):
- Subject: Easier access to new Redwood features — Beta sign-ups are getting simpler
- Body (short): We’re making it easier to try new features. Instead of waiting for an invite, you can join our beta waitlist and opt in for Early Access. If you want hands-on support and a committed SLA for evaluation, talk to your solutions contact about Priority Pilot. Learn more [link].

Internal Q&A / Anticipated questions (with suggested answers):
1) Q: Will existing invitees lose their access?
   A: No. Existing invitees receive an auto-qualify code during migration (Apr 6) that gives them Early Access. We’ll send personalized emails with next steps.

2) Q: What’s the difference between Early Access and Priority Pilot?
   A: Early Access = self-serve opt-in with telemetry and community support. Priority Pilot = assigned SE/CS support, limited capacity reservations, and optional NDA/contract.

3) Q: Does this change anything about data handling / privacy?
   A: No changes to our default data policies. We are adding explicit telemetry opt-in during sign-up and configurable data retention for Priority Pilot customers. Legal is reviewing wording.

4) Q: Will this increase load on hosted infra?
   A: Likely yes — we expect more sign-ups but most will exercise small workloads initially. Infra and capacity teams will have a pre-warm plan (see linked playbook). We’ll gate model-heavy features behind quota limits to avoid noisy spikes.

5) Q: How do we prevent abuse (spam / automated sign-ups)?
   A: We’ll add rate-limits, CAPTCHA on sign-up, and early telemetry checks to identify anomalous bursts. Growth and infra will coordinate thresholds.

6) Q: How do Sales/CS request a Priority Pilot?
   A: Create JIRA PROD-PILOT-xxx, include customer use case and expected QPS, SE will triage and request capacity reservation. Template will be on Confluence.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm exact consent language with Legal by Mar 20.
- Finalize sign-up widget copy (growth + design).
- Capacity: do we need temporary extra quota in EU region for initial 2 weeks? SRE/Infra follow-up required.
- Migration email copy for existing invitees (Marco to draft).
- Update pricing page if we expose any usage tiers during Early Access. Finance review needed.

Who should review this draft first: Leah (CS), Marco (growth), Priya (devex/docs), Anil (infra contact).

Channel playbook (internal brief):
- Slack: #all-prod-updates for exec summary; #cs-handoff for CS operational notes; ping named SEs for priority deals.
- Email: targeted email to current invite list and partners on Apr 6.
- Console banner: single-line CTA to sign-up + link to FAQ (Apr 6).

Rapid fallback / contingency plan if we see overload after launch:
- Immediately throttle new sign-ups (disable widget).
- Move heavy models behind an "invite for model" flag and keep core exploration models open.
- Escalate to oncall infra SRE for immediate scaling; communicate to CS to delay any onboarding.

Notes to self for the announcement meeting (Mar 23):
- Bring the sign-up mockups and migration email.
- Confirm Legal check and infra readiness.
- Ask CS for the list of 10 priority customers who should be offered Priority Pilot.

Version history (scratch):
- v0.1 2026-03-07 initial brain dump.
- v0.2 2026-03-11 added Q&A and migration plan after sync with Marco.
- v0.3 2026-03-12 updated timeline and added contingency steps per infra input.

Misc quick links / refs (to transfer into final doc):
- Confluence: Beta Access Policy (TBD).
- JIRA: PROD-3421 (internal tracking for sign-up widget).
- Docs PR: github.com/redwood-inference/marketing/pull/78

----
Notes to self: keep tone customer-friendly and operationally honest. Don’t promise exact dates publicly until Legal + Infra sign-off.
